items.stem: Lowering a colour's saturation while keeping its value roughly constant is best achieved by:

options.text: Adding a small amount of its complement (or a neutral) rather than black or white
options.rationale: Correct: complements/neutrals desaturate without large value shifts.
White mainly raises value and cools.
Black mainly lowers value and can muddy hue.

options.text: Adding more of the same hue

items.explanation: Correct: complements/neutrals desaturate without large value shifts.

items.stem: Which TWO practices help a painting read clearly from across a room? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Establishing a strong, simplified value structure early
options.rationale: Correct: value structure carries legibility at distance.

options.text: Concentrating the sharpest edges and highest contrast at the focal point
options.rationale: Correct: edge/contrast hierarchy directs the eye.

options.text: Giving every area equal detail and contrast

items.explanation: Correct: value structure carries legibility at distance.

options.text: Completing a painting (or passage) wet-into-wet in a single session
options.rationale: Correct: alla prima means working wet-into-wet, typically in one sitting.

options.text: Building many thin transparent glazes over weeks
options.rationale: That is glazing, not alla prima.

options.text: Painting only with a palette knife
options.rationale: Alla prima is about timing, not a single tool.
